title: Two-stage calibration of a 6-axis force-torque sensor for robust operation in the Mars 2020 robot arm
authors: Ethan W. Schaler | James Wisnowski | Yumi Iwashita | Jeffrey A. Edlund | Jacqueline H. Sly | William Raff | Kristopher L. Kriechbaum | Matthew A. Frost | Ryan L. McCormick | Julie A. Townsend
locator: §3–4.4; Tables 1–2; Figs 7–9; JPL CL21_2256, May 24 2021 author manuscript
finding: Two bonded plate PRTs supply redundant temperatures. Standalone single and combined loads repeated at −70 to +22 °C. Integrated free-space reference comes from turret mass, CG, pose and stiffness model; tests at −60 to +27 °C. Derived 24 within-side figure comparisons. No sample streams were in this deposit.
rights: © 2021, all rights reserved (manuscript p.1). Public repository link and original contrasts.

title: Temperature Compensation Method for a Six-Axis Force/Torque Sensor Using a Gated Recurrent Unit
authors: Hyun-Bin Kim | Seokju Lee | Byeong-Il Ham | Keun Ha Choi | Kyung-Soo Kim
locator: arXiv author PDF, Fig 3; Tables II–IV and Fig 8
finding: Board-temperature history and weight-loading protocol. Tables II–III refer to experiments with no external force. Six-axis RMS contrasts extracted. Their direction labels disagree with the figure references in the surrounding text. In Table II the sequential MLP is better than GRU for Fz.
rights: Public author arXiv copy, IEEE journal; original contrasts and source links only.

title: Triboelectric tactile sensor for pressure and temperature sensing in high-temperature applications
authors: Yanhua Liu | Jinlong Wang | Tao Liu | Zhiting Wei | Bin Luo | Mingchao Chi | Song Zhang | Chenchen Cai | Cong Gao | Tong Zhao | Shuangfei Wang | Shuangxi Nie
locator: Figs 4d, 5b–e; electronic Source Data workbook and Methods
finding: Diaphragms separately transduce temperature and pressure. 100 kPa channel means use eight temperatures; every one of the 80 Fig 5c cells reappears in 5d and is reproduced by the published linear coefficients from 5e. 5b observed channel means differ from grid values.
rights: Publisher CC BY-NC-ND 4.0. Source workbook remains with publisher, repository provides original numeric checks and aggregate factual comparisons only. https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-nc-nd/4.0/

title: Curvature-Aware Calibration of Tactile Sensors for Accurate Force Estimation on Non-Planar Surfaces
authors: Luoyan Zhong | Heather Jin Hee Kim | Dylan P. Losey | Cara M. Nunez
level: bibliographic screening plus verified experiment files
locator: IEEE abstract and experiment repository readme.md §§2–4
finding: Paper abstract reports six daily objects; this repository README and all released hold directories cover five. Calibration has independent ATI Nano17 normal component and resistive signals on seven substrate curvatures. No thermal channels identified.
rights: IEEE. Public abstract only. Separate repository has a root MIT license.

title: Application of a Temperature-Dependent Load Prediction Method to a RUAG Six-Component Block-Type Balance
finding: 406 calibration points at 294 K; at 315 K the study separates 54 calibration and 38 check-load points. With both temperatures the 38 axial-force check residuals fall within ±0.25% capacity for both prediction methods. Dataset is a balance bench; individual point values were not released with the report.
rights: Public NTRS manuscript. Original annotations; the public distribution field does not specify an open data license.

title: Assessment of Temperature-Dependent Regression Model Terms of a RUAG Six-Component Block-Type Balance
finding: Same RUAG block-balance research family. Percent-contribution analysis of primary-load or primary-output by temperature-difference terms evaluates sensitivity changes; the work reuses the same physical bench and prior analysis.
rights: Public NTRS manuscript, link and original annotation only.

title: Regression Analysis and Calibration Recommendations for the Characterization of Balance Temperature Effects
locator: § on calibration recommendations, Step 1, p.15; NTRS:20180002963
finding: The authors recommend at least three distinct temperatures for their design and single-component loads at auxiliary temperatures under specified model assumptions. Distinguish the recommended schedule from the later two-temperature RUAG experiment.
rights: Public NTRS manuscript, link and original annotation only.

title: Impedance characteristics in iontronic tactile sensors enabling intrinsic temperature-pressure decoupling
authors: Funing Hou | Chenxing Mu | Qinghai Zhang | Qianqian Tian | Song Gao | Mengqi Shi | Gang Li | Dianpeng Qi | Wei Yu | Jixiao Liu | Shijie Guo
locator: Results Fig 4d,g and Methods on the tactile array
finding: A reference thermometer and known 0.5/1 kg weights supply separate test references on the thermostat. A dynamic decoupling experiment reports mean errors 0.5 °C and 11.2 kPa. Setpoint, force, perceived pressure and sensor temperature are different quantities; no six-axis trace.
rights: Publisher CC BY-NC-ND 4.0. Original annotations only. https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-nc-nd/4.0/

title: Intrinsic Force–Temperature Self-Decoupling Enables Human-like Tactile Sensing in a Soft Ionic Skin

locator: Calibration and electrochemical characterization sections, figures describing thermocouple, weights and tensile-machine setup; reference 50
finding: At a controlled 55 °C, six nominal forces 0/0.5/1/2/5/10 N were compared. A separate zero-force test has 25/40/55/70/85 °C. These two sweeps do not establish a fully crossed 30-condition grid.

title: A Sensory Soft Robotic Gripper Capable of Learning-Based Object Recognition and Force-Controlled Grasping
authors: Zhanfeng Zhou | Runze Zuo | Binbin Ying | Junhui Zhu | Yong Wang | Xin Wang | Xinyu Liu
locator: Author-hosted IEEE PDF; Fig 4A–D; issue Jan 2024
finding: Five replicate measurements at each graphed pressure for the gripper tactile calibration at ambient 25 and freezing −20 °C. The thermal condition is ambient, not a wrist strain-gauge body thermometer.

title: Disturbance Elimination for the Modular Joint Torque Sensor of a Collaborative Robot
authors: He Zhang | Wenlei Qin | Yongsheng Gao | Qiang Li | Zhigang Chen | Jie Zhao
finding: Modular joint sensor heated from 20 to 45 °C in 5 °C increments; peak thermal error changes from 0.38 to 0.08 N m. Reference torque sensor and magnetic brake used in separate 0–70 N m calibration. The cooling branch and a synchronized load/temperature grid are absent.
rights: CC BY 4.0 per publisher Crossref record. https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/
